strengths: Addresses a well-motivated and practically important bottleneck: the edge-centric activation memory and O(L^6) tensor-contraction cost of mainstream equivariant GNNs, providing a clear systems-level motivation grounded in the roofline/memory-wall literature.

The EAAS derivation is a nontrivial theoretical contribution: it carefully derives, via alignment to the z-axis and CG selection rules in both complex and real bases, an exact parity-dependent re-indexing rule that replaces dense CG contractions with sparse, permutation-like maps (Appendix B gives a full derivation and low-degree worked examples).

The proposed On-the-Fly Equivariant Attention kernel is a sensible and creative adaptation of FlashAttention-style online-softmax, tiled streaming computation to the equivariant/E2Former factorization, directly targeting the O(|E|) attention-weight materialization bottleneck left unresolved by the original E2Former.

Empirical evaluation is fairly broad: microbenchmarks of the tensor product (6x speedup) and kernel (20x TFLOPS, ~17-20x memory reduction), accuracy on SPICE and OMol25, inference throughput/OOM scaling up to 100k atoms, and a downstream MD/RDF validation, together giving a multi-angle picture of efficiency and usefulness.
Reasonable reproducibility effort in the appendices, including timing protocols, synthetic system generation methodology, and configuration flags used for benchmarking.
weaknesses: The code availability statement in the abstract is left blank ("The code is avalible at" with nothing following), which is a real reproducibility deficiency for a paper whose central claims rest on a custom Triton kernel.

Accuracy claims are overstated relative to the actual tables: e.g., in Table 1 eSEN-Cons achieves substantially better aggregate Energy/Force MAE (0.23/6.36) than both E2Former-V2 variants (0.53-0.57/7.80-8.27), and in Table 2 eSEN-sm-cons and UMA-S are best or second-best on several sub-domains (Forces, Metals). The text's claim of "superior performance" and "lowest Energy and Force MAE across most subsets" is not well supported by a careful reading of the full tables.

The central contribution is primarily an efficient/hardware-aware realization of the already-published E2Former factorization (Li et al., 2025); the algorithmic novelty is incremental (SO(2) sparsification + kernel fusion) rather than a new theoretical framework, and this should be weighed against the significance claims.

The naive "PyTorch" baseline used for the kernel throughput/memory benchmarks (Figure 4, Section 5.2) is not precisely specified (unlike the detailed protocol given in Appendix A for Figure 1), making the reported 20x/17-20x numbers harder to independently verify or contextualize.

Despite the title emphasizing "Linear Activation Memory," the paper does not directly report training-time memory/throughput scaling curves for the full model against baselines (E2Former-V1, EquiformerV2, etc.); the OOM table (Table 3) is inference-only, and the linear-memory claim is validated mainly via isolated kernel microbenchmarks rather than end-to-end training measurements.

No explicit numerical correctness check (e.g., comparing EAAS output against a dense e3nn CG tensor product on random inputs) is reported to empirically confirm the claimed exact equivalence, even though Figure 3 only compares speed, not numerical agreement.

Minor presentation issues: incomplete code-availability sentence, inconsistent capitalization/formatting (e.g., "figure 2"), and dense notation that could benefit from a summary diagram earlier in the method section connecting Eq. (5)-(10) to Figure 2 more explicitly.

strengths: Addresses a well-motivated and practically important bottleneck (edge-centric materialization) in equivariant GNNs, with a clear connection to the FlashAttention line of work.

The Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS) is a nontrivial theoretical contribution: it derives, via a careful SO(3)->SO(2) alignment argument and parity analysis of Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, an exact sparse re-indexing rule replacing dense tensor-product contractions. Proofs and worked low-degree examples are provided in the appendix (App. B, C), improving credibility of the claims.

The proposed On-the-Fly Equivariant Attention kernel with online-softmax streaming (Algorithm 1) is a sound systems contribution that plausibly generalizes FlashAttention-style memory savings to equivariant message passing while preserving exactness of the underlying aggregation.

Extensive empirical evaluation spanning accuracy benchmarks (SPICE, OMol25, OC20 S2EF-2M) and systems benchmarks (kernel TFLOPS/memory vs. neighbors/atoms, end-to-end component ablations, inference throughput scaling to 100k atoms), plus downstream molecular dynamics validation (water RDF, AlphaFold-initialized protein MD) that goes beyond typical force/energy MAE tables.

Reasonably strong reproducibility support: detailed appendices document dataset descriptions, training hyperparameters, benchmark protocols (timing, system generation, OOM handling), and pseudocode for the kernel.
Ablation (Table 4) cleanly isolates the separate contributions of EAAS and the fused kernel, showing both are needed and that the fused kernel is necessary to avoid OOM at scale.
weaknesses: The headline '20x higher TFLOPS' and Figure 1/3 comparisons are made against a 'naive PyTorch implementation' or 'Traditional EGNNs' baseline; Appendix J's own numbers show that dense FlashAttention-style SDPA achieves substantially higher raw TFLOPS than the proposed sparse kernel (e.g., ~38.6 vs ~1.95 TFLOPS at N=32768, D=64), meaning the compute-efficiency claim holds only relative to weak baselines and is primarily a memory-scaling win rather than a raw-throughput win; this nuance is not clearly conveyed in the abstract/main text.

The architectural change described in Appendix D -- replacing the explicit equivariant non-linearity on the edge value path (as in EquiformerV2/eSEN) with a non-linearity folded into the attention bias -- is a substantive expressivity trade-off that is justified only empirically (via aggregate MAE parity), without deeper analysis of when/why this substitution could lose angular expressivity.

Accuracy comparisons are not uniformly favorable: on OMol25 (Table 2), eSEN-sm-cons and UMA-S actually outperform E2Former-V2 on several individual domains/metrics (e.g., Force MAE), so the claim of 'matching eSEN-small' is only true in aggregate and somewhat glosses over per-domain variation.

It is unclear whether all baseline throughput/accuracy numbers in Tables 1, 2, and 5 were independently reproduced by the authors under identical hardware/training conditions or taken directly from the original papers; if the latter, cross-method comparisons (especially throughput on a specific H20 GPU) may not be fully controlled or fair.
No uncertainty quantification (error bars, multiple seeds) is reported for any of the accuracy or throughput results, making it hard to assess the statistical significance of reported improvements.
The repository link in the abstract is left blank, and while this may be an artifact of anonymization, it currently limits verifiability of the code/kernel release.

The paper does not discuss potential numerical precision or stability implications of the EAAS sparsification (e.g., interaction with FP32 vs. lower precision, or edge cases near poles/degenerate geometries) beyond a brief FP32 mention in Appendix J.

strengths: Addresses a genuine and well-motivated bottleneck (edge-centric memory/compute) in equivariant GNNs, building on the theoretical factorization of E2Former-V1.
The EAAS derivation (axis-alignment + Wigner-6j recoupling collapsing to sparse re-indexing) is mathematically careful, with full derivations and low-degree worked examples given in the appendix.
Broad experimental coverage: SPICE, OMol25, OC20 S2EF-2M accuracy benchmarks, plus qualitative MD validation (water RDF, AlphaFold-initialized protein refinement).
Reasonably thorough ablations isolating the contribution of EAAS vs. the fused Triton kernel, and a neighbor-density sensitivity study showing where the node-centric design helps or hurts.

Commendably honest appendix (J) directly comparing against dense FlashAttention/SDPA, revealing that the proposed kernel is actually several-fold *slower* in raw TFLOPS than dense SDPA at matched settings -- a level of self-disclosure that is good scientific practice even though it undercuts the headline claims.
weaknesses: The central efficiency claims are inflated by baseline choice: the abstract/Fig.1 '20x TFLOPS' and 'up to 20x speedup' figures are measured against a naive/unspecified PyTorch 'Traditional EGNN' implementation and are not benchmarked against strong existing systems (cuEquivariance, OpenEquivariance, dense FlashAttention) in the main text; Appendix J shows the fused kernel is markedly slower (up to ~60x in some regimes) than dense SDPA in raw TFLOPS, which is not surfaced or reconciled in the main narrative.
EAAS's own speedup over already-optimized baselines (OpenEquivariance, cuEquivariance) is modest (~1.5-3.6x), a much less dramatic improvement than the framing in the abstract/contributions suggests.

Accuracy claims of 'preserving predictive accuracy' are not well supported: on OMol25 Val-Comp, E2Former-V2 is clearly worse than eSEN-sm-cons on Biomolecules (1.01 vs 0.59) and Organics (1.26 vs 0.84), and worse than UMA-S on Organics energy; results are mixed rather than consistently competitive, undermining the 'preserves accuracy' narrative used to justify the efficiency trade-off.

The 'Traditional EGNNs' and some other baseline curves (Fig. 1, latency comparisons) are custom re-implementations rather than published, tuned systems, making the headline latency comparison less trustworthy; no indication that these baselines were optimized to a comparable degree as the proposed kernel.

MD simulation validation (RDF, TM-score) is purely qualitative with a single trajectory each, no quantitative error metrics, uncertainty, or multiple seeds/replicates, so claims of 'physically faithful MD' are only weakly substantiated.

The paper is primarily a systems/kernel-engineering contribution; the genuinely novel theoretical content beyond the prior E2Former-V1 factorization is limited to the EAAS re-indexing trick, which is a fairly incremental extension of known SO(3)->SO(2) axis-alignment ideas (eSCN, EquiformerV2).
No code link is actually provided in the released manuscript despite an explicit code-availability sentence in the abstract, raising reproducibility concerns.

Reported gains are concentrated in a regime (tens of thousands to 100k atoms) that is not the size of the datasets used for accuracy evaluation (SPICE/OMol25 systems are much smaller, up to ~350 atoms), so the practical relevance of the efficiency gains to the actual accuracy benchmarks used is unclear; the large-scale efficiency and the accuracy evaluations are essentially decoupled experiments.

strengths: Combines a principled algebraic reduction (EAAS: SO(3)→SO(2) axis alignment yielding sparse parity re-indexing, with full derivation and proofs in Appendix B-C) with a genuinely useful systems contribution (a fused Triton kernel implementing FlashAttention-style online-softmax streaming for node-centric equivariant attention), addressing a real and well-motivated bottleneck (edge materialization) in existing edge-centric EGNN architectures.

Broad and fairly thorough empirical validation: accuracy on SPICE, OMol25, and OC20 S2EF-2M; direct kernel micro-benchmarks against cuEquivariance/OpenEquivariance/e3nn; system-level TFLOPS/memory scaling curves; component ablation isolating EAAS vs. the fused kernel; a neighbor-density sensitivity study; and inference-throughput scaling comparisons against many contemporary baselines (eSEN, UMA, MACE, GotenNet, EquiformerV2, etc.).

Includes a downstream physical validation beyond standard benchmark MAEs — bulk water RDF and a 2ns MD simulation of a ~30k-atom AlphaFold-initialized solvated protein — which is a meaningful demonstration that the efficiency gains translate into practically usable, physically stable simulations at scales prior models cannot reach.

Reasonably transparent about the honest trade-offs in Appendix D (clarifying that value-path non-linearity is reorganized rather than eliminated) and Appendix J (honestly reporting that dense FlashAttention/SDPA is still substantially faster in raw TFLOPS at matched shapes, and that the 20x claim is relative to naive PyTorch, not an optimized dense baseline).

Detailed reproducibility documentation of training hyperparameters, benchmark protocols, and dataset descriptions in the appendix, which aids independent verification of experimental conditions even absent released code.
weaknesses: Novelty is incremental: the core factorization is inherited directly from E2Former-V1 (Li et al., 2025), and the main new ingredients — SO(2) axis-alignment sparsification (conceptually close to eSCN/EquiformerV2's SO(2) basis-change tricks) and FlashAttention-style kernel fusion — are established techniques being ported into this specific setting rather than fundamentally new ideas.

The abstract's headline claim ("20x higher TFLOPS than standard implementations") is only clarified deep in Appendix J to be relative to a naive/unfused PyTorch baseline; the paper's own Table 12 shows dense FlashAttention-style SDPA is substantially faster in absolute TFLOPS than the proposed sparse kernel at matched shapes, which meaningfully qualifies the headline efficiency claim and should be foregrounded rather than relegated to an appendix.

The "preserves predictive accuracy" claim is only partially supported by the data: in Table 2 (OMol25), E2Former-V2 is not best on several Force MAE columns (e.g., Electrolytes, Metals, Organics) and is worse than eSEN-sm-cons or UMA-S on multiple sub-metrics, and in Table 1 (SPICE) eSEN-Cons. beats E2V2-Cons on overall Force MAE; the abstract/text framing understates these mixed results.

The code repository link in the abstract is left empty ("Our released code can be found at"), which is a significant reproducibility gap given the complexity of the described fused Triton kernel and EAAS re-indexing logic — details that would be very difficult to reproduce from the paper's description alone.

The integration between EAAS re-indexing and the fused on-the-fly attention kernel (Section 4.4/Algorithm 1) is not fully specified — the per-edge alignment rotation D_R and its inverse appear central to EAAS but Algorithm 1 does not show where/how this rotation is computed or fused within the streaming kernel, leaving an implementation gap between the two main contributions.

No error bars, multiple seeds, or statistical significance testing are reported for the accuracy tables (Tables 1, 2, 8), making it hard to assess whether the reported accuracy differences (some quite small, e.g., 1.24 vs 1.27 in Table 2) are meaningful.
